points.title: Query definition
points.must: A query is a request to the database in SQL; a SELECT returns a result set (a table).

points.title: INSERT syntax
points.must: INSERT INTO Table (fields) VALUES (values); values in the same order, text in quotes, AUTO_INCREMENT key left out; several rows at once.

points.title: SELECT basics
points.must: SELECT * / chosen fields FROM table; DISTINCT removes duplicates — with examples.

points.title: SELECT columns, WHERE rows
points.must: SELECT chooses the columns, WHERE chooses the rows; the table itself is not changed (diagram or example result).

points.title: WHERE operators
points.must: =, <>, <, >, <=, >=, AND, OR, NOT, BETWEEN (inclusive), IN, LIKE with % and _, IS NULL — each with an example.

points.title: Worked example of SELECT
points.must: A task broken into columns → table → rows → the final query (e.g. vegetarian meals under 900 tenge).

points.title: AND vs OR
points.must: 'Books of A and B' means pub = A OR pub = B / IN (A, B); AND on one field returns no rows.

points.title: UPDATE syntax
points.must: UPDATE Table SET field = value [, field2 = value2] WHERE condition; calculation from the old value (price = price * 1.1).

points.title: UPDATE example with result
points.must: An UPDATE with WHERE and the rows before / after, showing only matching rows change.

points.title: DELETE syntax
points.must: DELETE FROM Table WHERE condition; removes whole rows, no field list; without WHERE all records go but the table stays.

points.title: WHERE warning
points.must: UPDATE / DELETE without WHERE affect every record; use the primary key for one record; test with SELECT first.

points.title: DELETE vs DROP
points.must: DELETE = DML, removes records, structure stays; DROP TABLE = DDL, removes structure and data; DROP COLUMN removes a column.

points.title: Common mistakes
points.must: At least two: missing quotes, SET after WHERE, DELETE field FROM, = with a pattern instead of LIKE, AND instead of OR.
